evidence.finding: Official site states ad-hoc/direct payment is available via ePowerDirect/eCharge+ using credit card or PayPal, and explicitly says ad-hoc price can vary from station to station and is shown only after selecting the charge point. No Mainzer Stadtwerke autostrom tariff is offered for public stations.
Mainzer Stadtwerke confirms operation of more than 164 charge points in the region and QR-code ad-hoc access without a contract.
BNetzA-derived operator snapshot (28.07.2026) lists about 95 charging facilities / 182 charge points for Mainzer Stadtwerke AG.

A current station attributed to Mainzer Stadtwerke AG at Rheinallee 41 exposes EVSE DE*ISE*E0005257, confirming that this physical operator uses the shared DE*ISE namespace on at least part of its estate.

Current station-level observations show 0.63 EUR/kWh on many AC sites and 0.80 EUR/kWh on some DC sites, but these are discovery evidence only and cannot override the official statement that direct prices vary by station.

cpos.reason: Official current information explicitly makes the ad-hoc price station-dependent. Sampled DE*ISE EVSEs and station-level current prices exist, but DE*ISE is already known to be a shared technical prefix used by multiple physical operators. No Mainzer-wide or DE*ISE-wide fallback is safe.
cpos.neededToComplete: Resolve each Mainzer Stadtwerke physical EVSE to the public ePowerDirect/eCharge+ checkout and capture the exact current price plus any session/time/blocking component per EVSE; keep DE*ISE fail-closed by physical operator.

cpos.canonicalOperator: Erneuerbare für Marburg-Biedenkopf GmbH & Co. KG

evidence.finding: Official current page states that since 01.01.2024 all public charging stations in Landkreis Marburg-Biedenkopf are operated through the 100%-owned subsidiary Erneuerbare für Marburg-Biedenkopf GmbH & Co. KG; ad-hoc activation remains supported and the page links the price sheet.

The official price sheet currently linked by the operator is dated valid from 01.01.2025 and states ad-hoc 0.45 EUR/kWh, 1.00 EUR start fee, and 0.05 EUR/min blocking fee between 08:00-18:00 starting 60 minutes after charging ends.

January 2026 official magazine states EfMB operates 51 public stations / 102 charge points in Marburg and 80 stations / 160 charge points across the district, confirming the subsidiary as the current physical operating identity.
BNetzA-derived snapshot as of 28.07.2026 lists EfMB as the district's largest operator with 93 charging facilities.
Current third-party station observation shows 0.50 EUR/kWh plus 1.00 EUR start fee and 0.05 EUR/min blocking fee, conflicting with the still-linked official 2025 energy price of 0.45 EUR/kWh.

cpos.reason: The current official site still links a 2025 price sheet while current station-level observations show a higher energy price. This creates a freshness conflict that prevents safely treating 0.45 or 0.50 EUR/kWh as the 2026 network-wide direct price. The current eMI3 prefix is also not authoritatively established from available BNetzA-derived records.
cpos.neededToComplete: Obtain a current 2026 official price sheet or public ad-hoc checkout payload from EfMB/Stadtwerke Marburg, then map the exact tariff and eMI3 EVSE IDs to the 2026 BNetzA station inventory.

guardrails: No third-party current observation is promoted over an official tariff without resolving the freshness conflict.
No DE*ISE-wide price is created because the prefix is shared by multiple physical operators.
No Marburg eMI3 prefix is invented in the absence of authoritative mapping.
